name: Multi-resolution MPM for Large-domain Flooding
goal: Decide how to simulate a road vehicle crossing floodwater with MPM when the near-floor water-depth regime requires about 18 cells across a realised depth of 0.2944294473 m, giving dx about 0.01636 m, while a 30 x 12 x 3 m road-scale domain would need about 246.8 million background cells instead of 884,736 in the canonical tank. AT COARSE RESOLUTION, ABOUT 3.68 CELLS ACROSS THE DEPTH, ENFORCED-PLANE PENETRATION AND BOUNDARY SMEARING CORRUPT ROUGHLY 27 TO 72 PERCENT OF THE WATER COLUMN. THE DOMINANT MEASURED ERROR IS THEREFORE AT THE FLOOR BOUNDARY, NOT NECESSARILY AT THE VEHICLE. Explicitly search for a moving refinement window that follows a rigid body through a large domain, and report plainly if no such MPM demonstration exists. Use Steffen, Kirby and Berzins 2008 as a required anchor.
summary:
The literature contains credible local-resolution MPM for solids and free-surface fluids, but NO DEMONSTRATED MPM STUDY WAS FOUND THAT FOLLOWS A RIGID VEHICLE WITH A REFINEMENT WINDOW THROUGH A LARGE FLOOD DOMAIN; the closest fluid result is dynamic AMR for free-surface waves and breaking WITHOUT a vehicle [Mao16], while adaptive MPM-FSI work is preliminary and not road-scale flooding [Hu10].

CLOSEST STRUCTURAL MATCH: dynamic AMR [Mao16] and moving mesh management [Shi10] reduce active cells but DO NOT establish near-floor accuracy, particles-per-cell control, or moving-body refinement. GIMP/SAMRAI nested grids [Ma05], structured GIMP refinement [Ma06], mesh grading [Lia15], hierarchical B-spline MPM [Zha21g] and local BSMPM bridging [Sun20d] are PREDOMINANTLY SOLID-ONLY. [Zha21g] uses splitting, WHICH IS UNSAFE FOR HISTORY VARIABLES unless deformation-gradient transfer is defined.
MOST TRANSFERABLE COST REDUCTIONS: sparse active grids [Qiu22, Zha26s] and dynamic meshing [Shi10] cut memory and work when the domain is empty, BUT DO NOT REDUCE THE SMALLEST-CELL EXPLICIT TIMESTEP OR RESOLVE THE FLOOR LAYER. Hybrid 3-D MPM / 2-D shallow-water coupling [Pan23c] and MPM-finite-volume depth-averaging [Zhe23d] address FAR-FIELD cost, not vehicle-scale near-floor physics.
[Ste08] IS DECISIVE: fixed particles-per-cell can LOSE convergence under grid refinement. Methods must co-refine or control PPC, otherwise AMR silently changes quadrature and transfer conditioning. Standard MPM, GIMP, CPDI and B-spline MPM CANNOT BE TREATED INTERCHANGEABLY; nonuniform grids already produce projection error [Wal07], and boundary stability can impose harsher CFL limits [Bai22, Ni20].
ADJACENT: adaptive SPH supplies the strongest moving-body precedent, splitting, merging, shifting and geometry-following refinement [Mut21, Hu18, Haft22], but its remedies require reformulation for MPM's deformation gradient and history-dependent stress. NO MOVING-REFERENCE-FRAME MPM RESULT WAS IDENTIFIED; open-boundary MPM exists [Zha19e].
